correctness.rationale: Run-root/excess bijection gives each exact one-symbol duplication as a one-coordinate increment. For any adjacent pair, solving adjacency to both proves exactly two incompatible orientations for every third member; coordinate minima/maxima recover unique parameters for all cliques of size at least three. Stars and bars counts both types; binomial derivatives yield the triple formula and shifted relation. Clique-size and common-read bounds use exact run counts. Direct alphabet-word enumeration corroborates every triple in tested ranges and all higher sizes in smaller ranges.

value.rationale: Higher-order decoding ambiguity is not captured by the graph edge count: pairwise-confusable triples may or may not share any received string. The theorem gives the complete, naturally parameterized classification and exact census of both cases at every clique size over all word lengths and alphabets. The linear gap between maximum pairwise clique size and maximum simultaneous-parent list size quantifies a real distinction relevant to list reconstruction; no arbitrary parameter slice or unmotivated table. This is a structural all-length result rather than an isolated finite census.
